The 'Ron Wyld Shield', presented for the very first time, went to Mark Sinclair. The competition is an extremely hard one to win for it is gained through points awarded during the whole of the winter season for racing AND training!
The points competition for the Ron Wyld award has begun again and I am sure this will be a closely fought competition as already the boys are following the points situation with great interest.
Mark won the Boys Cross Country Championship in 1976 and was placed 3rd this year. He was winner of the Ron Wyld award last season.

Six likely lads, in appropriate dress gave a fine exhibition of the art of sprinting!! - props provided by Ron Wyld and Brian Pritchard. There was a disputed finish - if only they had had photo finish equipment in 1887!
Ron Wyld eventually recovered it from the Games Village so it will still be around this year. On the track the final of the 100 was the highlight.
This was emphasised when Ron and Ann Wyld booked a table for 15 to celebrate their 30th wedding anniversary and over twice that number turned up.

Ron Wyld too has found his way over here and lives a few kilometres north of me. I bumped into Ron a while back in the NSW Academy of Sport weights room, puffing and blowing on a rowing machine whilst Steve Smith and Brendan Reilly stood there laughing at him.

The Shippens soon met up with Ron Wyld and helped him to celebrate his 60th birthday along with other guests Dave Scott, Joy Gardener (Pete's mother), and Scott Wyld and almost before Clive's feet had touched the floor he was being inveigled into helping to coach pole vault at Homebush Stadium.
